chunks: And from him, from Ayoub, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar and Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who said:

He was asked about a man who missed one rak'ah of the Maghrib prayer with the Imam, so he caught the two (remaining) rak'ahs; the first is his and the second is for the congregation, and he sits for the tashahhud in it. He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And the second (rak'ah) as well?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'All of them?' He said, 'Yes, and they are merely a blessing.'
ai.seo_question: How does a worshipper count their rak'ahs if they join the Maghrib prayer late and miss only one unit?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudence of *jamāʿah* (congregation) by affirming that a latecomer who misses only one rakʿah of Maghrib with the Imam counts that single rakʿah as their own, while the subsequent two rakʿahs are shared with the congregation. The Imam’s affirmation that 'it is all for him' and 'it is merely a blessing' highlights the Shia scholarly view that the extra rakʿahs serve as a spiritual grace (*barakah*) rather than a rigid structural requirement, facilitating ease for the worshipper. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the integration of individual and communal prayer components.
